newsitem.title: FRANCE: French frost grips grapes in Cotes-du-Rhone.
newsitem.headline: French frost grips grapes in Cotes-du-Rhone.

text.p: Frost has damaged about a fifth of the vines in the Cotes-du-Rhone region of southern France after one of the worst spring freezes in decades, the local wine producers' association said on Monday.
About 8,000 hectares (20,000 acres) of the 45,000 hectares (110,000 acres) of vineyards in the region, mostly in the south of the Drome region, were hit by frost overnight on Thursday.
In the worst-affected area, the Coteaux de Tricastin, about 80 percent of the tiny grapes in the vineyards were hit by frost.

"It's very serious in some areas. Production this year will be down but it's too early to say how much," said Sylvie Reboul of the Cotes-du-Rhone wine-growers' association based in Avignon, southern France.
She said the frost was apparently the worst in the region since 1972. Some reports said it was the most extensive since 1945. Some vineyards to the south of the Cotes du Rhone were also hit.
Frost, of about minus five Celsius (23F), was more damaging than normal for this time of year because an unseasonably early spring meant vines had flowered three weeks ahead of season.

"Until May 10 or 11 there is still the possibility of further frosts," Reboul told Reuters. She said that 8,000 hectares would normally produce about 400,000 hectolitres (8.8 million Imp gallons) of wine.
She said growers were asking local government authorities to declare an "agricultural disaster" that would enable them to qualify for emergency aid.

France has also been hit by a dry spell this spring that has hit plantings, cut river levels and led to fears of crop-wilting drought. "If it doesn't rain in the next 10 days there will be very serious damage," said Jean-Pierre Grellier of France's largest farm union, FNSEA.
